title: Ratchet a tie-down strap taut round a crate and latch its handle before the deck is jolted
instruction: Strap the crate down to the deck.
context: Drivers and loaders secure each item before a vehicle moves. Cargo-securement rules and ratchet makers' operating instructions agree: take up the strap with full strokes of the ratchet handle until it is tight, then close the handle flat until it locks. A handle left up can be knocked or flung open to its release position and let the strap go, and a slack strap lets the load shift when the vehicle brakes. Here the crate stands on a deck section with a slack strap round it; after the robot lets go, the deck runs into a hard stop. Unlike #1026 (turn a tourniquet windlass to a gauge mark, then clip the rod), tension comes from repeated lever strokes held by a pawl, the lock is that same handle pressed flat past its detent, and the proof is a physical jolt. Unlike #890 (ratchet strokes drive a bolt) and #256 (pump strokes to a pressure), the job ends by latching the operating lever. Done by: light truck drivers; freight and material movers (O*NET 53-3033.00, 53-7062.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table; heights above the deck's top. Deck section: a steel chequer plate 24 x 24 x 1 cm centred at x 29, y -11, its top 1.2 cm above the table, ballasted underneath so it and its carriage move 20 kg in all, on a linear slide along x: 15 cm of travel from a rear stop (the start) to a steel end stop in front. On it, all bolted to the plate: a painted plywood stake board 1.2 cm thick, 10.6 cm wide, 12 cm tall, centred at x 24.9, y -7.5 (front face at x 25.5); a steel anchor stake 1.2 x 1 x 11.5 cm tall at x 26.2, y -1.0; a steel lever ratchet for 3 cm webbing, mounted on its side on a steel post 2.6 x 1.6 x 8 cm at x 26.6, y -14.5, so its mandrel and handle pin are vertical, the pin at x 26.2, y -14.5, 9 cm up, the mandrel's cheek at x 26.8, y -13.4. A wooden (pine) crate, ballasted to 1 kg, 5.5 cm front to back, 10 cm wide, 14 cm tall, centred at x 28.3, y -7.5, stands against the stake board. The tie-down (orange polyester webbing 3 cm wide, 100 g, its centre line 9 cm up) runs 23.3 cm from the anchor stake to the ratchet: a 5.95 cm leg along the crate's left side at y -1.95 (4 mm clear), 11.4 cm across its far face (12 mm off it, at x 32.4), and a 5.95 cm leg along its right side at y -13.05 into the ratchet's mandrel at x 26.6. The ratchet handle (steel lever 7.2 cm long, 60 g) carries a red PVC-sleeved grip post 1.2 x 1.2 x 3.6 cm at 6.4 cm from the pin; it stands 40 deg open (0 is shut flat along the strap, toward the robot; it opens away from the crate).
scoring: From the poses of the deck, crate, band and handle (on a real rig: the strap's tension on a load cell under the anchor stake, the handle's angle on a protractor plate round its pin, and the crate's position on the deck from video against marks). Taut = 50 N or more in the strap. In sim the tension is modelled, not measured: each full stroke (handle out past 75 deg, then back under 35 deg) winds 5 mm, and tension = 8 N per mm wound beyond the band meeting the crate (4 strokes give about 60 N, 3 about 20 N); on a real rig the load cell reads it (calibration in the README). Latched: pressed to within 1 deg of shut, and within 1.5 deg now. The trip: once both grippers have been 3 cm clear of the crate, strap and handle and everything still for 1 s, the deck runs 15 cm into its stop at about 0.38 m/s; it is over 1 s after the stop. Fail, latched for the trial (score 0): the handle opened to 150 deg (strap let out), the crate moved over 3 mm or 2 deg before the trip, or over 2.5 mm or 2 deg on the deck during it. Score: 0.25 for taut; with that, +0.25 for latched; with both, +0.5 once the trip is over. Halved unless both grippers are 2.5 cm clear of the crate, strap and handle and they are still. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Engage the deck's catch first. Pull the ratchet's release and pay the strap out to its slack mark (12 mm off the crate in sim; on a real rig the mark set at calibration so 3 full strokes read under 50 N and 4 read 50 N or more), set the handle 40 deg open, stand the crate against the stake board, and run the deck back by hand onto its rear stop (raising the drive weight) until the catch holds it. Real rig: the deck is pulled by a weight of about 1 kg on a cord over a pulley (about 10 N, set so it reaches the stop at 0.38 m/s), held by a catch that fails safe (stays engaged without power), inside a fixed guard with an e-stop; the load cell is zeroed with the strap slack. Calibration, the stop and the guarding are in the README.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2/1.0). The strap is a rigid band on a slider with an 8 kN/m spring (webbing stretch); a per-step pawl rule winds 5 mm per full handle stroke. The handle is a friction hinge; a per-step detent rule pushes it out below 12 deg until pressed within 1 deg, then holds it latched; opened to 150 deg it frees the strap. The jolt: the deck, a 20 kg slider body, runs into its end stop; an unlatched handle's friction is off for 0.4 s after.
